kid.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar boast about as he walked in his palace?

options.text: Conquering Egypt with his new army
Building Babylon by his own power
Feeding Judah from his own fields
Restoring Jerusalem with his royal treasure

kid.explanation: The king credited Babylon's greatness to his power and the honor of his majesty.

kid.question: What happened while the king's boast was still being spoken?

options.text: A heavenly voice announced his kingdom's departure
A palace guard announced his successor's arrival
A foreign envoy announced his kingdom's expansion
A royal messenger announced his army's victory

kid.explanation: A voice from heaven announced that the kingdom had departed from him, followed by his life among beasts.

kid.question: How did the king live after being driven from people?

options.text: He ate grass like the oxen
He caught fish beside the river
He grew wheat beside the palace
He begged bread beside the gates

kid.explanation: He was driven from men, ate grass like oxen, and was exposed to the dew.

kid.question: What happened when Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven?

options.text: His soldiers returned from war
His treasures returned from Egypt
His understanding returned to him
His children returned from exile

kid.explanation: He reports that his understanding returned and he blessed and praised the Most High.

kid.question: What happened to his position as king?

options.text: He was sent to serve another king
He was made governor of a distant province
He was replaced by one of his counselors
He was established in his kingdom again

kid.explanation: His reason, honor, and brightness returned, his officials sought him, and he was established in his kingdom.

kid.question: What did Belshazzar bring to his feast for drinking?

options.text: Cups brought by Egypt's trading ships
Bowls borrowed from Babylon's poorest families
Vessels taken from Jerusalem's temple
Jars gathered from the army's camps

kid.explanation: He ordered the gold and silver vessels taken from the Jerusalem temple to be used for drinking wine.

kid.question: What appeared during the feast?

options.text: A bird speaking beside the palace window
Fingers writing on the palace wall
A sword floating above the banquet table
A flame burning on the royal throne

kid.explanation: Fingers of a hand wrote on the plaster wall opposite the candlestick.

kid.question: How did Belshazzar react to the writing?

options.text: He became sleepy and left the banquet
He became frightened and his knees shook
He became joyful and ordered more wine
He became angry and dismissed the musicians

kid.explanation: His thoughts troubled him, his appearance changed, and his knees struck together; the failed interpretation increased his alarm.

kid.question: Who recommended calling Daniel to explain the writing?

options.text: The queen
The captain
The steward
The herald

kid.explanation: The queen entered the banquet house and described Daniel's proven understanding and interpretive gifts.

kid.question: What did Daniel say about the offered rewards?

options.text: Delay them; the priests must explain
Share them; the magicians will explain
Increase them; I will explain afterward
Keep them; I will still explain

kid.explanation: Daniel told the king to keep his gifts or give them to another, while agreeing to read and interpret the writing.

high-school.question: How does the heavenly announcement answer the king's boast?

options.text: It divides the kingdom he claimed to have shared with his counselors
It enlarges the kingdom he claimed to have inherited from his father
It secures the kingdom he claimed to govern on behalf of heaven
It removes the kingdom he claimed to hold by his own power

high-school.explanation: His boast about personal power is interrupted by the declaration that the kingdom has departed until he learns the Most High rules.

high-school.question: How does the restored king describe the lesson he learned?

options.text: Babylon's priests can restore those who master its rituals
Courtly wisdom can protect those who choose skilled advisers
Heaven's King can humble those who walk in pride
Royal armies can preserve those who strengthen their borders

high-school.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar praises God's enduring dominion and concludes that He can abase those walking in pride.

high-school.question: How does restoration relate to the king's new view of power?

options.text: His recovered rule follows acknowledgment of God's unrestrainable will
His recovered rule follows victory over the invading armies
His recovered rule follows acceptance of the counselors' new treaty
His recovered rule follows payment to the dream-interpreting priests

high-school.explanation: The king acknowledges that no one can stay God's hand, then recounts the return of reason and royal authority.

high-school.question: What makes the banquet's use of temple vessels religiously significant?

options.text: Sacred vessels are used while material gods receive praise
Sacred vessels are returned while Jerusalem's priests receive tribute
Sacred vessels are repaired while court officials restore temple worship
Sacred vessels are hidden while foreign armies search the palace

high-school.explanation: Belshazzar uses vessels from God's temple for wine while praising gods made of metals, wood, and stone.

high-school.question: What happens after the reward for interpreting is announced?

options.text: The wise men fail and the king grows more troubled
The wise men compete and the king postpones the decision
The wise men flee and the king orders the gates closed
The wise men agree and the king crowns their leader

high-school.explanation: Despite the promised scarlet, gold chain, and third rulership, the wise men cannot read or interpret the writing.

high-school.question: Why does the queen recommend Daniel?

options.text: His record includes victories and directing provincial armies
His record includes wisdom and explaining difficult matters
His record includes royal descent and governing Babylon
His record includes temple rebuilding and priestly service

high-school.explanation: She recalls his understanding, dream interpretation, and ability to explain hard matters during Nebuchadnezzar's reign.

high-school.question: How does Daniel respond to the king's proposed exchange?

options.text: He agrees to interpret if the earlier wise men first endorse him
He agrees to interpret without accepting the reward as his condition
He agrees to interpret when the banquet guests return the temple vessels
He agrees to interpret after receiving authority over all the provinces

high-school.explanation: Daniel tells the king to keep the gifts or give them elsewhere, yet says he will read and interpret.

high-school.question: Why does Daniel recount Nebuchadnezzar's loss of authority?

options.text: It proves Daniel's right to inherit the previous ruler's throne
It explains the queen's failure to protect the previous ruler
It establishes the army's power to remove the previous ruler
It shows divine judgment on pride in the previous ruler

high-school.explanation: Daniel recalls power granted by God, a heart lifted in pride, deposition, and eventual recognition that God rules.

high-school.question: What makes Belshazzar accountable in Daniel's rebuke?

options.text: He heard the earlier warning but had mistaken Daniel's identity
He knew the earlier lesson but had not humbled his heart
He taught the earlier lesson but had lost the temple vessels
He lacked the earlier records but had attempted their translation

high-school.explanation: Daniel explicitly says Belshazzar knew all this yet had not humbled his heart.

high-school.question: What contrast exposes Belshazzar's misplaced worship?

options.text: He praises provincial governors while ignoring the soldiers defending his palace
He praises foreign priests while dismissing the magicians trained by his father
He praises unseeing idols while dishonoring the God holding his breath
He praises ancestral rulers while refusing the queen's counsel about royal succession

high-school.explanation: The gods of materials cannot see, hear, or know; the God who holds his breath and ways has not been glorified.

expert.question: How does the timing sharpen the reversal of Nebuchadnezzar's claim?

options.text: The boast is still being spoken when heaven declares his loss of rule
The boast is repeated by counselors before the people invite him back to rule
The boast is first recorded after heaven announces his restoration to rule
The boast is withdrawn by the king before heaven confirms his right to rule

expert.explanation: The voice falls while the word is in his mouth, and the announced humiliation is fulfilled that same hour.

expert.question: What changes between the king's opening boast and closing praise?

options.text: Personal boasting gives way to praise of the queen's role in government
Personal boasting gives way to praise of the army's authority over succession
Personal boasting gives way to praise of the heavenly King's supremacy
Personal boasting gives way to praise of Daniel's right to the throne

expert.explanation: He first credits his own might and majesty, then praises the King of heaven and His power to abase pride.

expert.question: Which ordering describes the recovery account?

options.text: He regains kingship, praises his counselors, looks heavenward, and recounts military victories
He looks heavenward, regains understanding, praises God, and recounts restored kingship
He looks heavenward, appoints a successor, praises the army, and recounts lost understanding
He regains understanding, rebuilds the palace, praises his counselors, and recounts restored worship

expert.explanation: His heavenward look and returning understanding lead into praise; he then describes the restoration of reason, honor, and kingdom.

expert.question: How does the narrative juxtapose royal celebration and vulnerability?

options.text: The feast's display of status is interrupted by a dispute that disperses the lords
The feast's display of status is interrupted by writing that physically unnerves the king
The feast's display of status is interrupted by an invasion that removes the queen
The feast's display of status is interrupted by a drought that empties the vessels

expert.explanation: The banquet before a thousand lords and use of temple vessels are followed by the hand's writing and the king's bodily fear.

expert.question: What basis for finding an interpreter succeeds the court's failed summons?

options.text: The queen recalls Daniel's earlier record of interpreting difficult matters
The queen increases the promised reward for the same specialists
The queen supplies the palace scribes with an older translation
The queen recommends consulting Jerusalem's priests about the sacred vessels

expert.explanation: After the wise men fail, she recommends Daniel on the basis of his known interpretive wisdom in the earlier reign.

expert.question: What evidence does Daniel 5:19 use to illustrate the king's granted majesty?

options.text: He could kill or spare and elevate or bring down whom he chose
He could determine provincial boundaries and redistribute fields among the families he chose
He could appoint foreign priests and set their festivals throughout the lands he ruled
He could name the rulers of Media and assign the royal offices of Persia

expert.explanation: Daniel says God gave Nebuchadnezzar majesty that made peoples fear him, then describes his discretion over life, death, advancement, and demotion.

expert.question: How does the recollection explain both royal greatness and its removal?

options.text: The people grant authority and remove it when their allegiance changes
The army grants authority and removes it when the ruler loses battles
The priests grant authority and remove it when the ruler changes rituals
God grants authority and removes it when the ruler hardens in pride

expert.explanation: Daniel attributes Nebuchadnezzar's greatness to God, then links his pride with deposition until he recognized God's rule.

expert.question: What is the force of telling Belshazzar that he knew all this?

options.text: Knowledge of the predecessor's humiliation excuses the delay in seeking an interpreter
Knowledge of the predecessor's humiliation explains his ability to read the writing
Knowledge of the predecessor's humiliation establishes his hereditary claim to Jerusalem
Knowledge of the predecessor's humiliation heightens responsibility for his own pride

expert.explanation: Daniel contrasts Nebuchadnezzar's learned acknowledgment with Belshazzar's failure to humble himself despite knowing the history.

expert.question: How do the two sides of Daniel's accusation differ in agency?

options.text: Manufactured gods direct the banquet; the dishonored God speaks only through ancestors
Manufactured gods lack perception; the dishonored God sustains the king's life
Manufactured gods preserve the kingdom; the dishonored God governs only distant peoples
Manufactured gods control the vessels; the dishonored God guards only the temple

expert.explanation: Daniel calls the material gods unable to see, hear, or know, while placing Belshazzar's breath and ways in God's hand.

expert.question: What contrast emerges between the two rulers' responses to divine authority?

options.text: The restored ruler rejects divine humbling; the informed successor orders faithful worship
The restored ruler denies divine rule; the informed successor praises the heavenly King
The restored ruler praises divine humbling; the informed successor repeats defiance
The restored ruler transfers royal power; the informed successor refuses the offered throne

expert.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar ends by praising God's power to humble pride; Daniel rebukes Belshazzar for refusing humility despite knowing that lesson.
